extracted.intended_audience: NYC agencies, agency rulewriters, municipal attorneys, mayor's office staff, city council staff, and regulated parties seeking to understand CAPA rulemaking and adjudication requirements
extracted.subtask_description: A compact of New York City administrative procedure requirements (City Administrative Procedure Act) governing agency rulemaking, regulatory agendas, publication and notice, review processes, emergency rules, compilation of rules, adjudications, and declaratory rulings. Targets agency compliance with statutory procedures and public-participation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Adjudication” means a proceeding in which the legal rights, duties or privileges of named parties are required by law to be determined by an agency on a record and after an opportunity for a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Agency” means any one or more of the elected or appointed officers provided for in this charter and any other official or entity which is acting (1) under the direction of one or more of such officers, (2) under the direction of one or more other officials who are appointed by, or appointed on the recommendation of, such officers, or (3) under the direction of a board, the majority of whose members are appointed by, or appointed upon the recommendation of, one or more of such officers, but shall not include the city council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Compilation” means the Compilation of city rules required to be published under section one thousand forty-five.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Law” means federal, state and local law, this charter, and rules issued pursuant thereto.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule — general definition
rubrics_metrics.description: “Rule” means the whole or part of any statement or communication of general applicability that (i) implements or applies law or policy, or (ii) prescribes the procedural requirements of an agency including an amendment, suspension, or repeal of any such statement or communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statutory definition frames what counts as a rule for CAPA purposes and is the starting point for applying the Act's procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule — inclusive examples (what a rule includes)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Rule” shall include, but not be limited to, any statement or communication which prescribes (i) standards which, if violated, may result in a sanction or penalty; (ii) a fee to be charged by or required to be paid to an agency; (iii) standards for the issuance, suspension or revocation of a license or permit; (iv) standards for any product, material, or service which must be met before manufacture, distribution, sale or use; (v) standards for the procurement of goods and services; (vi) standards for the disposition of public property or property under agency control; or (vii) standards for the granting of loans or other benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule — exclusions (what is not a rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Rule” shall not include any (i) statement or communication which relates only to the internal management or personnel of an agency which does not materially affect the rights of or procedures available to the public; (ii) form, instruction, or statement or communication of general policy, which in itself has no legal effect but is merely explanatory; (iii) statement or communication concerning the allocation of agency resources or personnel; (iv) statement or communication for guiding, directing or otherwise regulating vehicular and pedestrian traffic ... the determination and installation of which is based on engineering or other technical considerations not involving substantial policy considerations; (v) statement or communication effecting a noncontinuous closing of a street; or (vi) statement or communication adopted pursuant to sections [listed sections] except pursuant to certain clauses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists categories of communications excluded from CAPA's rule definition; practitioners should read the exclusions carefully when deciding whether CAPA procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda — annual publication and required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall publish by the first day of May annually, a regulatory agenda which shall contain: (1) a brief description of subject areas in which rules may be promulgated during the next fiscal year and reasons; (2) a summary, to the extent known, of anticipated contents of each proposed rule, its objectives and legal basis; (3) a description of the types of individuals and entities likely to be subject to the rule; (4) an identification, to the extent practicable, of all relevant federal, state, and local laws and rules, including duplications/overlaps/conflicts; and (5) an approximate schedule for adopting the proposed rule and the name and telephone number of an agency official knowledgeable about each subject area involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must prepare an annual roadmap for expected rulemaking; the agenda must be reasonably specific about subjects, affected parties, legal authorities, potential conflicts, and scheduling and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mayoral review of agency regulatory agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency the single head of which is appointed by the mayor shall forward to the mayor its regulatory agenda. The mayor shall review such regulatory agenda to determine whether regulations contemplated by city agencies are consistent with the policy objectives of the administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking on matters not in the regulatory agenda — requirement to state reason
rubrics_metrics.description: If rulemaking is undertaken on a matter not included in the regulatory agenda the agency shall include in the notice of proposed rulemaking the reason the rule was not anticipated. The inadvertent failure to provide the reason shall not serve to invalidate the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may still promulgate rules not listed in the agenda, but must explain in the notice why the item was not included; harmless omissions are not fatal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and plain-language drafting requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency is empowered to adopt rules necessary to carry out the powers and duties delegated to it by or pursuant to federal, state or local law. No agency shall adopt a rule except pursuant to this section. Each such rule shall be simply written, using ordinary language where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules must be within delegated authority and drafted in simple, ordinary language when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and form of notice — publication in City Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall publish the full text of the proposed rule in the City Record at least thirty days prior to the date set for a public hearing or the final date for receipt of written comments, whichever is earlier. A proposed rule amending an existing rule shall contain in brackets any part to be deleted and shall have underlined or italicized any new part to be added. A proposed rule repealing an existing rule shall contain in brackets the rule to be repealed, or if the full text was published in the Compilation, shall give the citation and a summary of its contents. Such notice shall include a draft statement of the basis and purpose, the statutory authority (particular sections and subdivisions), the time and place of public hearing or reason no hearing, and the final date for receipt of written comments. If not included in the regulatory agenda, the notice shall include the reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies exact publication timing, formatting conventions for amendments/repeals, and mandatory contents of the notice of proposed rulemaking (statement of basis and purpose, authority, hearing info, comment deadline, and agenda-omission reason if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of proposed-rule copies to government and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of the full text of the proposed rule shall be electronically transmitted to the office of the speaker of the council, the council’s office of legislative documents, the corporation counsel, each council member, the chairs of all community boards, the news media and civic organizations no later than the date the proposed rule is transmitted to the City Record; provided that an inadvertent failure to fully comply with the notice requirements of this paragraph shall not serve to invalidate any rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must proactively send copies to key city officials and stakeholder groups; harmless technical failures do not invalidate the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'news media' and 'civic organizations' for notice purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: News media includes all radio and television stations broadcasting in the city, all newspapers published in the city having a citywide or boroughwide circulation, any newspaper of any labor union or trade association representing an industry affected by such rule, and any community newspaper or other publication that requests annual notification. Civic organizations include any citywide or boroughwide organization or any labor union, trade association or other group that requests such notification on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the universe of entities entitled to receive proposed-rule transmissions when agencies are complying with notice obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Website posting and online publicity requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall provide information regarding the public hearing in a prominent location on its website at least seven days prior to the date set for such hearing, and provide a prominent link to the NYC Rules online portal (or successor). Each agency shall, to the greatest extent practicable, publicize upcoming public hearings via electronic means likely to reach interested members of the public. This paragraph does not create a private right of action and inadvertent failure to comply shall not invalidate any rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must use their websites and online portals to publicize hearings and link to the central rules portal; this is a public-notice best-practice requirement rather than a privately enforceable right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporation counsel review of delegated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The corporation counsel shall review the proposed rule to determine whether it is within the authority delegated by law to the agency proposing the rule. If not within delegated authority, the corporation counsel shall notify the agency in writing prior to publication of the final rule in the City Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An intra-governmental legal check to ensure agencies do not exceed statutory authority; written notice required before final publication if a problem is found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law department and mayor’s office of operations review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The law department shall state whether each proposed rule: (i) is drafted so as to accomplish the purpose of the authorizing provisions of law; (ii) is not in conflict with other applicable rules; (iii) to the extent practicable and appropriate, is narrowly drawn to achieve its stated purpose; and (iv) to the extent practicable and appropriate, contains a statement of basis and purpose that provides a clear explanation of the rule and the requirements imposed by the rule. The mayor’s office of operations shall analyze: (a) whether such rule is understandable and written in plain language; (b) how the drafting process included analysis sufficient to minimize compliance costs for the discrete regulated community or communities, consistent with achieving the stated purpose; and (c) why, if the rule establishes or modifies a violation or penalty without a cure period, such cure period or other opportunity for ameliorative action was not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dual substantive review: law department focuses on legality, conflict, narrowness, and clarity of basis/purpose; operations focuses on plain language, cost-minimization for affected communities, and justification for omitting cure periods when penalties/violations are involved. There are carve-outs (see exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and public annexing of review analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing review, the law department and the mayor’s office of operations shall certify that they have performed such review, and shall promptly transmit a copy of such certification, including the analysis, to the relevant agency. The agency shall annex such certification and analysis to the full text of the proposed rule as published in the City Record and make it available to the public on the city’s website and transmit it to the speaker of the city council at the time of publication. No proposed rule shall be submitted for initial publication in the City Record unless such certification and analysis have been issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must attach intra-governmental review certification/analysis to proposed rules and publish them publicly; compliance is a precondition to initial City Record publication (with enumerated statutory exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to review and certification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The review and certification subdivision shall not apply to rules that: (i) are promulgated pursuant to emergency procedures; (ii) are solely concerned with establishing/modifying monetary penalty amounts where the underlying violation or penalties have been analyzed previously; (iii) are solely concerned with establishment/modification of fees; or (iv) implement particular mandates or standards set forth in newly enacted federal, state, or local laws, regulations or other requirements with only minor exercise of agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates routine or emergency exceptions where full law-department/operations review is not required; if analysis is not performed under these exceptions, that fact must be noted and annexed to the proposed rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for public comment and agency outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall provide the public an opportunity to comment through: (i) outreach to the discrete regulated community or communities, if one exists; (ii) submission of written data, views, or arguments; and (iii) a public hearing unless the agency determines in writing that such a hearing would serve no public purpose (such determination shall be published in the notice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must actively solicit comments from affected communities and accept written and oral input; the agency must explain in writing and in the notice if it declines to hold a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public record of comments and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: All written comments and a summary of oral comments concerning a proposed rule received from the public or any agency shall be placed in a public record and made readily available to the public as soon as practicable and in any event within a reasonable time, not to be delayed because of continued pendency of consideration of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must maintain and publish the public record of comments and summaries of oral testimony promptly; open-record access is required and cannot be deferred due to ongoing deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final-rule posting before adoption by boards/commissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Other than a rule adopted pursuant to emergency procedures, no final rule shall be adopted by a board or commission unless its final language is posted in a prominent location on the agency's website and electronically transmitted to each member of the board or commission at least three calendar days, exclusive of Sundays, prior to such rule's adoption; revisions may be made prior to the vote if approved by unanimous consent of the members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a notice period for boards/commissions to review final language; allows unanimous-consent last-minute edits but otherwise requires public posting in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness conditions and 30-day publication rule
rubrics_metrics.description: No rule shall be effective until: (a) filed by the agency with the corporation counsel for publication in the Compilation; (b) the rule and statement of basis and purpose are transmitted to the council for its information; (c) in the case of rules adopted pursuant to local law, the effective date of the local law provision has occurred; and (d) the rule and statement of basis and purpose have been published in the City Record and thirty days have elapsed after such publication. The thirty-day requirement does not apply where a finding of substantial need for earlier implementation is made in writing by the agency and approved by the mayor and contained in the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the sequence and preconditions for a rule's legal effectiveness, including a presumptive 30-day waiting period after City Record publication and required transmittals to corporation counsel and the council; mayor-approved emergency need can shorten this period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voidance and delayed-publication cure for omitted publication
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule shall be void if it is not published in the next supplement to the Compilation in which its publication is practicable; however, in the case of an inadvertent failure to publish, the rule shall become effective as of the date of its publication if published within six months of the corporation counsel receiving notice of its omission. Judicial or administrative actions commenced under a rule voided pursuant to this section and pending prior to such voidance may be prosecuted and defended to final effect as if the rule had not been voided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication timing is critical: failure to include a rule in the next practicable supplement can void it, but there's a six-month cure for inadvertent omissions; pending actions are preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for rulemaking by any person
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may petition an agency to consider the adoption of any rule. Within sixty days after submission, the agency shall either deny the petition in writing stating reasons, or state the agency’s intention to initiate rulemaking by a specified date concerning the subject of such petition. Each agency shall prescribe by rule the procedure for submission, consideration and disposition of such petitions. For multi-member bodies, procedures may authorize delegation to the chair to reject petitions. Such decision is within the agency's discretion and not subject to judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a right to request rulemaking and prescribes a prompt agency response timeline; agencies must adopt procedures for petitions, and petition denials are discretionary and generally not reviewable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and public availability of comments system
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall establish a system for maintaining and making available for public inspection all written comments received in response to each notice of rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational requirement to store and provide access to public comments on proposed rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule adoption procedures and findings
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency may adopt a rule prior to notice and comment if immediate effectiveness is necessary to address an imminent threat to health, safety, property or a necessary service. A finding of imminent threat and specific reasons must be made in writing by the agency and approved by the mayor (unless another elected official has authority), and the rule and finding must be made public forthwith and published in the City Record as soon as practicable. Agencies shall electronically transmit emergency rules to specified officials and stakeholders no later than the date the emergency rules are transmitted to the City Record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency authority is tightly constrained: written finding, mayoral approval (except for other elected rulemakers), immediate public disclosure, and prompt transmission to government and stakeholder recipients are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency-rule duration and extension limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule adopted on an emergency basis shall not remain in effect for longer than sixty days unless the agency has initiated notice and comment required by the section within such sixty-day period and publishes with such notice a statement that an extension of the rule on an emergency basis is necessary for an additional sixty days to afford an opportunity for notice and comment and to adopt a final rule; provided that no further such finding of an emergency may be made with respect to the same or a substantially similar rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency rules are time-limited (60 days) and can be extended once for an additional 60 days only if notice-and-comment is initiated; repeated emergency renewals for the same substantive rule are precluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of previously adopted rules — agency submission and classification (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: By specified historical deadlines (e.g., by August 10, 1989), each agency was required to send the corporation counsel copies of each rule in force as of January 1, 1989, and to identify each as: (a) continued in present form, (b) continued with amendments, or (c) repealed. Any amendment or repeal of such a rule is subject to the rulemaking provisions of section 1043.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historic transitional obligation to catalog existing rules and classify them for continuation, amendment, or repeal; modern practitioners should note this was a one-time submission requirement tied to CAPA's implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corporation counsel duties on submitted prior rules (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: The corporation counsel shall include submitted rules in the Compilation, publish notations for rules identified for amendment or repeal, and submit to the City Record for publication a list of rules submitted (with short descriptive titles and identifying information) by specified historical deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes corporation counsel's publication and notification duties in the CAPA transition period; included for completeness though many deadlines are historical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compilation of city rules — publication, certification, and update obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The corporation counsel shall publish a Compilation of city rules and keep it up to date through supplements issued at least every six months and at other appropriate times. The Compilation and its supplements shall be certified by the corporation counsel and shall include every rule currently in effect. The Compilation shall be organized by agency and indexed by subject matter. An indexed edition was to be published by July 1, 1991 and updated every fourth year thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the official, certified repository of city rules, the cadence for updates (at least semiannual supplements), and organizational/indexing expectations; certification makes the Compilation authoritative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and nonsubstantive revisions in the Compilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials included in the Compilation may be edited, rearranged and updated for clarity, accuracy and reorganization without change in substance. Section numbers, stylistic and organizational formats and other nonsubstantive revisions effected by the law department pursuant to this subdivision shall become effective on the publication date of the Compilation and upon the publication of each supplement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows editorial/nonsubstantive modernization in the official Compilation without triggering the rulemaking process, but such changes are effective upon publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing/access for documents not formally adopted as rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents submitted by an agency pursuant to the review of previously adopted rules which were not formally adopted by the agency as rules shall either be included in the Compilation or filed in the municipal reference and research center in an easily accessible form. Notice of such filing and a list of the documents shall be published in the City Record. Such documents so filed shall, if otherwise valid, continue to be effective, but any amendment or repeal of any document within the definition of rule shall be in accordance with section 1043.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a pathway for non-rule agency documents to be made publicly accessible and clarifies that substantive changes to materials that qualify as 'rules' must follow formal rulemaking procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — notice content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall be given reasonable notice of such hearing, which shall include: (1) a statement of the nature of the proceeding and the time and place it will be held, if applicable; (2) a statement of the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held, and a reference to the particular sections of the law and rules involved; and (3) a short and plain statement of the matters to be adjudicated, including reference to the particular sections of law and rule involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum content for hearing notices so parties understand the proceeding, legal basis, and issues to be decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — notice of agency procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall adopt rules governing agency procedures for adjudications and appeals. Agencies shall make a copy of any such rule available, upon request, to any party who has received notice of violation of the laws, rules or orders enforced by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires agencies to have and provide access to procedural rules governing adjudications and appeals when parties are notified of violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — hearing rights and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall be afforded an opportunity for a hearing within a reasonable time. At the hearing parties shall have due process including the opportunity to be represented by counsel, to issue subpoenas or request their issuance, to call witnesses, to cross-examine opposing witnesses and to present oral and written arguments on law and facts. Adherence to formal rules of evidence is not required. No ex parte communications relating to other than ministerial matters regarding a proceeding shall be received by a hearing officer, including internal agency directives not published as rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees basic procedural protections and adversarial rights in agency adjudications while allowing flexibility from strict evidentiary rules; prohibits substantive ex parte communications to hearing officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — findings, burden of proof, and record reliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings of fact shall be based exclusively on the record of the proceeding as a whole. Except as otherwise provided by state or local law, the party commencing the adjudication shall have the burden of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates record-based factfinding and places the initial burden on the initiating party absent other law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — transcript/record access
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing shall be transcribed or recorded and a copy of the transcript or record, or any part thereof, shall be made available to any party upon request. A typed or recorded copy of such transcript shall be provided upon request for a reasonable cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures availability of the hearing record to parties for review, appeal, or enforcement, subject to reasonable copying costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — informal disposition allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless precluded by law, informal disposition may be made of any matter which is the subject of an adjudication by methods of alternative dispute resolution, stipulation, agreed settlement, or consent order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages use of ADR and settlement mechanisms to resolve adjudicative matters where legally permissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — hearing officer assignment, role, and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as otherwise provided for by this charter the person presiding at a hearing shall be assigned solely to adjudicative and related duties. Such hearing officer shall make final findings of fact and shall not make any final decision, determination, or order, but shall only recommend such, and shall forward such recommendation and the record of the adjudication to the agency, who may adopt, reject or modify any such recommended decision, determination or order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separates factfinding (hearing officer) from agency decisionmaking: hearing officers make findings and recommendations; the agency takes the final action unless charter exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — required content and delivery of recommended/final decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any recommended decision, final decision, determination or order shall be in writing, or stated in the record if the parties are present, and shall include findings of fact and conclusions of law. A copy of any written recommended decision, final decision, determination, or order shall be delivered or mailed forthwith to each party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must articulate factual findings and legal conclusions and be promptly communicated to the parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parking Violations Bureau exception
rubrics_metrics.description: The parking violations bureau shall not be subject to the requirements of Section 1046 (Adjudication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit carve-out: adjudication procedural requirements do not apply to parking violations bureau proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory ruling procedure and binding scope
rubrics_metrics.description: On the written petition of any person, an agency may issue a written declaratory ruling on the applicability of any rule adopted by it, to any person, property, or state of facts. A declaratory ruling shall be binding only with respect to the person who makes the petition and only with respect to the stated facts contained in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a mechanism for individuals to obtain agency interpretations of rules; rulings are narrowly binding only to the petitioner and the petition's factual scenario.
